Inglewood, California
  July 30, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, July 30, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
  Authority, Finance Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.
  The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/  Housing Authority
  Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary/Joint Powers  Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman/Finance  Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council  Members/Successor  Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/Finance
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk/Acting Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Jeffrey Lewis  Sr. Assistant City Attorney/Sr. Assistant General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Cheryl Moore  Management Assistant

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  lottery process and the following people were selected:

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded
  by Mayor Butts that the City Council does hereby amend the criteria to reflect that
  the lottery selection list will be good for three years. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council can identify other sources to extend the program to
  others. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts that
  the demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority
  dated, July 25, 2019, in the amount of $20,359,096.88, are hereby allowed, and
  the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is
  hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Mayor Butts collectively called for the Public Hearings regarding the maintenance
  assessment districts (Agenda Item Nos. PH-1 through PH-4).

  2
 July 30, 2019

 183  PUBLIC HEARINGS HELD - INITIATE PROCEEDINGS FOR THE
  ANNUAL LEVY AND COLLECTION OF ASSESSMENTS FOR: 1)
  MORNINGSIDE PARK MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO.
  1974-2; RESOLUTION NO. 19-98 ADOPTED (PH-1); 2) IN-TOWN
  MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1975-1; RESOLUTION
  NO. 19-99 ADOPTED (PH-2); 3) INGLEWOOD STREET LIGHTING
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1980-1; RESOLUTION NO. 19-100
  ADOPTED (PH-3); 4) DARBY DIXON MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT
  DISTRICT NO. 1987-1; RESOLUTION NO. 19-101 ADOPTED (PH-4). The
  Acting City Clerk announced the next scheduled matters are a public hearing to
  initiate proceedings for the annual levy and collection of assessments for the
  Morningside Park Maintenance Assessment District No. 1974-2; A public hearing
  to initiate proceedings for the annual levy and collection of assessments for the
  In-Town Maintenance Assessment District No. 1975-1; A public hearing to
  initiate proceedings for the annual levy and collection of assessments for the
  Inglewood Street Lighting Assessment District No. 1980-1; and a public hearing
  to initiate proceedings for the annual levy and collection of assessments for
  Darby-Dixon Maintenance Assessment District No. 1987-1; and that notices were
  given in the time, form and manner as required by law, and no communications
  were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff reports dated July 30, 2019.

  Louis A. Atwell, P.E., Assistant City Manager, gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the
  City Council on the Assessment Items called collectively (PH-1 through PH-4).

  Ray Davis commented he would like to see more money allocated for the
  downtown area.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:43 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 19-
  98 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  MODIFYING  AND/OR
  APPROVING THE ENGINEER’S REPORT, ORDERING
  IMPROVEMENTS AND THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF
  ASSESSMENTS WITHIN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  MORNINGSIDE PARK ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1974-2

  2) Adopt Resolution No. 19-99 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  MODIFYING  AND/OR
  APPROVING THE ENGINEER’S REPORT, ORDERING
  IMPROVEMENTS AND THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF
  ASSESSMENTS WITHIN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, IN-
  TOWN MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1975-1

  3) Adopt Resolution No. 19-100 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  MODIFYING  AND/OR
  APPROVING THE ENGINEERING REPORT, ORDERING
  IMPROVEMENTS AND THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF
  ASSESSMENTS WITHIN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  3

  STREET LIGHTING ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1980-1

  and; 4) Adopt Resolution No. 19-101 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA  MODIFYING  AND/OR
  APPROVING THE ENGINEER’S REPORT, ORDERING
  IMPROVEMENTS AND THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF
  ASSESSMENTS WITHIN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  DARBY-DIXON MAINTENENACE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT
  NO. 1987-1
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor
  Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  131.8  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – DRAFT FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN. The Acting City Clerk announced that the next scheduled
  matter is a public hearing to approve the Draft Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Annual
  Action Plan, that notice was given in the time, form, and manner as required by
  law, and that no communication was received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated July 30, 2019.

  Robert Chavez, Housing Manager, gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the
  City Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the City Council does hereby approve the Draft Fiscal Year
  2019-2020 Annual Action Plan. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor
  Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 142  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-016 APPROVED –
  MESQUEMAI,  INC., dba: OLYMPIQUE  FAÇADE  ACCESS
  CONSULTING FIRM. Staff report dated July 30, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 19-016 with
  Mesquemai, Inc., dba: OLYMPIQUE Façade Access Consulting Firm, extending
  the term to June 30, 2020.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to
  Agreement No. 19-016. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 19-257 APPROVED – LOS ANGELES REGIONAL
  INTEROPERABLE  COMMUNICATIONS  SYSTEM  (LA-RICS)
  AUTHORITY. Staff report dated July 30, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval of an Agreement with the Los Angeles Regional Interoperable
  Communications System (LA-RICS) Authority.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-257. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;

  4
 July 30, 2019

  and
  Noes:  None.

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 19-256 APPROVED – JOSEPHSON INSTITUTE OF
  ETHICS. Staff report dated July 30, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval of an Agreement (with an option to extend an additional year) with the
  Josephson Institute of Ethics for training and coaching services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-256 (with an
  option to extend an additional year) with the Josephson Institute of Ethics for
  training and coaching services. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 178  FISCAL YEAR 2020 OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY GRANT
  AUTHORIZED AND ACCEPTED. Staff report dated July 30, 2019, was
  presented recommending authorization to accept the Fiscal Year 2020 Office of
  Traffic Safety Grant.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby: 1) Authorize acceptance of the FY
  2020 Office of Traffic Safety Grant in the amount of $260,000; and 2) Direct that
  said funds be budgeted as part of the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Budget. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 131.8  EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT NO. 19-258 APPROVED –
  THOMAS SAFRAN & ASSOCIATES DEVELOPMENT, INC. Staff report
  dated July 30, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an Exclusive
  Negotiation Agreement between the City of Inglewood, the Inglewood Housing
  Authority and Thomas Safran & Associates Development, Inc., for the property
  located at 716-720 West Beach Avenue.

  It was moved by Council Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and
  seconded by Council Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 219  CITY TREASURER – MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report
  dated July 30, 2019, was presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for
  the Month ending April 30, 2019.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

 126.1  APPOINTMENT TO CIVIL SERVICE REVIEW COMMISSION
  RATIFIED – AT-LARGE. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and
  seconded by Council Member Padilla that Tina McKinnor be appointed to the
  Civil Service Review Commission representing the City at-large for the term
  ending July 2020. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  5
 July 30, 2019

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Ray Davis, 2nd District inquired if there is any rehab money for units that need to
  be fixed up.

  Brandon (No last name given), representative from Assembly Woman Autumn
  Burke, invited the residents of the 62nd Assembly District to her Back to School
  Health and Wellness event happening at Crozier Middle School 120 W. Regent
  Street, Inglewood, CA, on August 3, 2019, from 10:00 a.m. until 3:00 p.m.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned in honor of Margie Neal Garrett at the hour of 3:04 p.m.

  Approved this day of 1st of October, 2019
